convention: The held friction coefficient is a material's coefficient against itself, where an attested self-pair stands (wood on wood, steel on steel, ice on ice, glass on glass); the engine's mixing law (the square root of the product of the two fixtures' coefficients) governs cross pairs in stepping. Attested pair values that are not self-pairs (brick on wood, cast iron on steel, wood on stone) do NOT decompose into self-coefficients without inventing a decomposition, so where a self-coefficient rests on such a pair the value is the intake's authored point at the pair's value, and its source line says so. A consequence, recorded: an attested pair value need not be reproduced by the mixed computation (wood on stone computes to about 0.49 from the held self-coefficients, against the table's 0.2); pair readings proper (design note §3.2) are the remedy when a question turns on a specific pair, and are not in this intake.
